en: You must be quite taken with this town, eh?
I hope that Calstatt,
with so many people staying here like this,
will be a good town for them.
Please, stay in this town
for as long as you like.
When you come by, even my work
feels more worthwhile.
I hear the mayor's son is quite a handful.
"He won't listen to a word I say!"
the mayor was fretting.
, isn't it?
note: Name is printed at the end of msg 94930 ('You're, uh...' #2408 / NAME); this row follows it: 'NAME, isn't it?'

en: It's lonely when I haven't seen you lately.
I work at City Hall, you know.
If you need anything, come to City Hall
note: Followed by shared #2415 (slice 030), which must complete it, e.g. 'any time.'

en: Good day.
note: Shared: Martin/Wolf greeting, Christine farewell; 'Good day.' works both ways

en: Well, we do keep running into each other.
I see. Thank you.
If you have time, why not go have a look...
That's kind of you. Thank you.
Are there any empty houses in this town?
I hear the mayor's son has turned over a new leaf!
"He's become such a kind boy,"
the mayor said. He was so pleased.
You know this town well.
Now you will use that knowledge for me.
At this hour.
What brings you here so late at night?
You know this town well, so
Ah, I understand.
You've had trouble finding a place to stay.
Maybe it's the ship that came in recently, but

en: every hotel seems to be full.
Given the hour,
please, stay at my place tonight.
No, I couldn't...
It's quite all right.
note: Printed on the same line as #2517: trailing space

en: Don't you worry about it.
I'll get a bed ready for you right now.
Sorry to keep you waiting.
Well, it's work again tomorrow. Let's get to bed.
Good night, then.
(Forgive me, Martin.)
Aaaagh
Ahh, I am your servant...
Hey, good morning.
I'm just heading off to work at the factory.
The work is hard and grueling...
I'm off to work at the factory now.
The work is hard and grueling, but
if I don't work, I don't eat.
Another day of work

en: It's so tough, it's going to wreck my health.
Lately
note: Msg 99044 ends here; msg 99060 continues with #180 '...'

en: going to the factory's gotten a bit more fun.

en: My sweetheart works at the same factory.
I'm Kürten.
What business could a fine gent like you
possibly have with me?
Factory work sure is rough...
Haaah.
I'm completely worn out.
If I came home to a wife waiting for me,
I bet that would make me happy.
Maybe I should get married after all...
Hello, I'm Kürten.
Can I help you with something?
No, I seem to have the wrong house.
I've only just come to this town, so...

You wouldn't have business with the likes of me, right?
Ah,
You came all the way to my house to hear
